Why a BRICS Gold Standard Is a Fiction

Since the sanctions on Russia over the invasion of Ukraine, combined with real domestic economic anxieties in the post-pandemic era and declining institutional trust, a handful of libertarians and a mix of anti-war conservatives and the far-left have been announcing that de-dollarization was inevitable, driven by BRICS’s desire to pursue a gold-backed currency.

candidates.author: David Morgan
candidates.text:
TMR has factored this into our thinking on #Platinum. 
For every ounce of platinum mined, the world mines roughly 19 ounces of gold.

Platinum’s rarity does not automatically make it more expensive, however. Gold has a much larger monetary and investment demand base, while platinum prices are heavily influenced by automobiles, industrial activity, recycling, and South African mine supply. Platinum is the rarer metal; gold remains the stronger monetary metal.
